title: Solar Panel Wattage Calculator (kWh to Watts) | Wattlyst
meta: Find the total solar panel watts you need from daily kWh and your city's sun hours. Losses included; shows the number of 585W panels.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: How many watts of solar panel do I need?
p: Take the units on your bill, turn them into units a day, and divide by what one kW of panels really makes a day where you live. For 300 units a month in Lahore that is 9.9 units a day ÷ 4 = 2.47 kW of panels. The yield figure already includes the losses from heat, dust, wiring and the inverter, so you do not add another margin on top.

The calculator then rounds up to whole panels of the size you chose: 5 panels of 585 W, or 2.93 kW installed, which makes about 355 units a month. The extra over your bill is normal; the next whole panel always adds a little.

sections.h2: Solar panel size calculator: does panel wattage matter?
p: The total watts are fixed by your units; the panel size only changes how many panels and how much roof. 2.47 kW is 5 panels of 585 W on 12.9 m², 5 panels of 550 W on 12.8 m², or 7 panels of 400 W on 13.7 m². Larger panels mean fewer frames, clamps and cables, so installers prefer them when the roof is open.
Smaller panels help when the roof is cut up by water tanks and stairs, because a whole panel is lost each time one does not fit. Pick the size from the quote and let the calculator count.

sections.h2: What is the daily output of a 585 W panel?
p: A 585 W panel does not make its label watts all day. In Lahore one such panel makes about 71 units a month over the year, a little over two units a day, more in May and June and less in December and January. In Karachi or Quetta the same panel makes more because the sun is stronger. This is the solar panel output the calculator uses when it divides your units by the yield.
If a quote promises far more units per panel than this, it is quoting a clear summer noon, not a yearly average.

sections.h2: How many solar panels for 9.9 units a day?
p: 9.9 units a day is 300 units a month, the default above: 5 panels of 585 W in Lahore, 2.93 kW. The same 9.9 units a day in Karachi need 4 panels (2.34 kW) because each kW makes 4.7 units a day there. For any other daily figure, multiply by 30.42 and enter it as monthly units, or use the solar system size calculator, which takes daily kWh directly.

sections.h2: Solar watts calculator for a bigger bill
p: The watts grow in a straight line with the units: 1,000 units a month in Lahore is 32.9 units a day and needs 8.23 kW, 15 panels of 585 W on about 38.7 m² of roof. Above five kW the connection and net-billing rules change, so check the sanctioned load with your DISCO before buying.

This page sizes panels from the units you use. It does not check whether the panels can carry your AC at noon without the grid; for that, size from the appliance list with the solar system from loads calculator.

faq.q: How many watts of solar panels do I need for 300 units a month?
faq.a: About 2.47 kW in Lahore: 5 panels of 585 W, 2.93 kW installed, on about 12.9 m² of roof. Karachi needs 4 panels for the same bill because of its stronger sun.

faq.q: How many solar panels for 9.9 kWh a day?
faq.a: 9.9 kWh a day is 300 units a month, so 5 panels of 585 W in Lahore or 4 in Karachi. Multiply any daily figure by 30.42 to enter it as monthly units.

faq.q: How much power does a 585 W solar panel produce per day?
faq.a: About 71 units a month in Lahore as a yearly average, a little over two units a day, after heat, dust, wiring and inverter losses. Summer days make more, winter days less.

faq.q: Does a bigger panel wattage mean fewer panels?
faq.a: Yes, for the same total: 2.47 kW is 5 panels of 585 W, 5 of 550 W or 7 of 400 W. The total watts and the units made stay about the same.

faq.q: Why does the installed kW come out higher than the calculated kW?
faq.a: Because you cannot buy a fraction of a panel. 2.47 kW needs 5 whole panels of 585 W, which is 2.93 kW. The extra makes a few more units a month.

faq.q: Is this a solar panel output calculator too?
faq.a: Yes, in reverse: the units a month shown for each size is what that array should make in your city as a yearly average. One 585 W panel in Lahore makes about 71 units a month.

faq.q: What else do I need besides the panel watts?
faq.a: An inverter sized for the running load of the house, a charge controller or hybrid inverter if you add a battery, and DC cable sized for the string current and run. Use the inverter size, charge controller size and solar DC cable calculators next.

key_facts: Solar panel wattage for a home = daily units ÷ the units each kW of panels makes a day in the city: 300 units a month in Lahore is 9.9 units a day and needs 2.47 kW of panels, or 5 panels of 585 W.
One kW of panels makes about 4 units a day in Lahore and 4.7 in Karachi over the year (Global Solar Atlas), so the same bill needs 5 panels in Lahore but 4 in Karachi.
One 585 W panel makes about 71 units a month in Lahore as a yearly average, after real-world losses; 60 units a month of usage is covered by exactly 1 panel.
Panel size does not change the total watts: 2.47 kW is 5 panels of 585 W or 7 panels of 400 W, but the smaller panels take 13.7 m² of roof instead of 12.9 m².
mistakes: Dividing by the panel's label watts and the hours of daylight. A panel makes its rated watts only at a clear noon; use the yearly yield per kW, which the calculator takes from your city's sun data.
Sizing from a winter bill. Pick the bill for the months you want covered; a summer bill with the AC can be two or three times a winter one.
Counting the roof as free. 5 panels need about 12.9 m² with walkways, and a shaded corner costs a whole panel's output.

Expecting the panels to run the AC at noon by themselves. This page matches energy over the month; whether the array can carry the running load at midday without the grid is a separate check in the solar system from loads calculator.
Ignoring the sanctioned load. Net billing is capped at the sanctioned load of the connection, so a large array may need a bigger connection first.

msg.city_unknown: We do not have sun data for this city yet. Pick the nearest city or enter the yield yourself.
msg.usage_required: Enter your monthly units or daily kWh.
msg.yield_or_city_or_psh_required: Pick a city or enter peak sun hours.
msg.appliance_unknown: Pick an appliance from the list, or choose Custom and enter its watts.
msg.other_start_below_run: Starting watts of the other loads cannot be lower than their running watts.
msg.loads_hours_required: Enter hours per day for at least one appliance.
msg.drive_above_standard_sizes: This drive is above the largest size we list. Use one larger solar pump drive rated for this motor (two drives cannot share one motor) and ask the supplier or a licensed engineer; the size shown is the calculated minimum.
msg.motor_v_invalid: Pick the motor voltage from the list: 220 V single-phase or 400 V three-phase.
msg.string_below_bus: The panels in series are capped by the drive's maximum DC input on a cold morning, so on hot afternoons the string gives less than the voltage the motor needs at full speed and the pump runs slower then (see the string voltage in the working). Check the drive's DC input range with the supplier.
msg.above_standard_sizes: This is above the largest standard size we list. Split the array or circuit into two, or ask a licensed electrician or engineer; the sizes shown are the calculated minimums.
msg.generator_above_standard_sizes: This is above the largest generator size we list. Use two generators on separate circuits or a larger industrial set, and ask a licensed electrician; the size shown is the calculated minimum.
msg.forecast_unavailable: The live forecast is not available right now, so a typical day is shown. Try again later.
msg.usage_both: Both boxes are filled, so the units a day are used and the monthly units are left out. Clear the daily box to size from your bill.
msg.typical_used: Blank boxes in your list use the typical value for that appliance (its listed watts and hours a day, quantity 1). Type your own numbers for an exact result.
msg.internal_non_finite: These numbers are outside a realistic range. Please check your inputs.

examples.title: 300 units a month with 400 W panels
examples.text: Same 2.47 kW, but at 400 W a panel it takes 7 panels, 2.8 kW installed on 13.7 m² of roof. More panels, more mounting and cable, same energy.

examples.title: 300 units a month in Karachi
examples.text: Karachi makes 4.7 units per kW a day, so 9.9 ÷ 4.7 = 2.12 kW: 4 panels of 585 W, 2.34 kW installed, about 331 units a month.

examples.title: What one 585 W panel makes in Lahore
examples.text: 60 units a month is 2 units a day, which needs 0.49 kW, so exactly 1 panel of 585 W. That panel makes about 71 units a month as a yearly average, a little more than the 60 needed.

examples.title: 1,000 units a month in Lahore
examples.text: 32.9 units a day ÷ 4 = 8.23 kW. 15 panels of 585 W, 8.78 kW installed on about 38.7 m² of roof, making about 1,066 units a month.

content.answer: For a bill of 300 units a month in Lahore you need about 2.47 kW of solar panel wattage, which is 5 panels of 585 W (2.93 kW installed) on about 12.9 m² of roof. Panel watts = daily units ÷ the units one kW of panels makes a day in your city, rounded up to whole panels.

formula.text: E = units_month ÷ 30.42; kW = E ÷ yield; panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel); kW_installed = panels × W_panel ÷ 1000
lines: yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city (losses included)
kW = total panel capacity needed (thousands of watts)
W_panel = watts of one panel; panels are rounded up to a whole number
Roof area = panels × area of one panel

content.safety: Panels on a roof produce dangerous DC voltage in daylight even when switched off at the inverter; the DC wiring, isolators, earthing and grid connection must be done by a licensed electrician or a certified solar installer.
